c1-29.title: Making a film
c1-29.story: Max and Sofia decided to shoot a short film for the school festival, and Anna offered to help. The [[casting]] took place in Anna's living room, where Taras auditioned for the role of a grumpy pirate. Max set up his old camera on a [[tripod]] so the shots would stay steady. Anna acted as [[production designer]], turning the kitchen into a pirate ship with blankets and cardboard. The story opened with a [[flashback]] to the pirate's childhood, with Taras in a paper hat. Their favorite [[gag]] involved the family cat stealing the pirate's sandwich. Grandpa insisted on a brief [[cameo]] as a mysterious old sailor. When they watched the [[footage]] that evening, everyone laughed until they cried. At the festival, the final [[close-up]] of the cat licking its whiskers got the loudest cheer of the day.

c1-30.title: Hollywood hits
c1-30.story: On Friday night, Anna and her friends argued about what to watch. Lisa wanted the latest superhero [[blockbuster]], while Ira insisted that its [[sequel]] was even better. Max, who considers himself a film expert, suggested an old black-and-white [[noir]] with rainy streets and a mysterious detective. Anna's mama laughed and said she preferred a good [[melodrama]] with plenty of tears. Before they could decide, a [[promo]] appeared on TV for a [[spin-off]] about the superhero's clumsy sidekick. Its catchy [[jingle]] stuck in everyone's head for the rest of the evening. Max complained that [[show business]] only cares about money and that the [[mainstream]] never takes risks. In the end, they voted, and the superhero movie won four to one. Max sulked for five minutes, then hummed the tune louder than anyone.

c1-31.title: Fantasy and sci-fi
c1-31.story: Taras invented a board game that mixed fantasy and science fiction, and he made the whole family play it on Sunday. Dad chose to be a [[mage]] who could freeze enemies with a single spell. Mama played a friendly [[ogre]] who guarded a bridge and asked travelers riddles. Grandpa, as usual, wanted to be the villain, an [[orc]] king with an army of noisy [[minions|minion]]. Grandma secretly played an [[android]] that looked completely human, and nobody suspected her. Halfway through, the heroes met a little [[droid]] that beeped loudly at every wrong move. The final enemy was a [[cyborg]], half man and half machine, who guarded a magic pond. Anna, who studies biology, pointed at a tiny creature Taras had drawn in the pond. She said it was a [[hydra]], just like the ones she had seen under a microscope. Grandpa admitted that cherry pie was his [[kryptonite]], so Grandma bribed him with a slice and won the whole game.

c1-32.title: A startup's new app
c1-32.story: Max and his sister Sofia spent the summer building an app that helps students swap used textbooks. Sofia handled the [[web design]], choosing calm colors and big, friendly buttons. Max worked on the [[back end]], connecting the app to a free [[API]] that looked up book prices automatically. Because their budget was tiny, they relied heavily on [[open source]] libraries written by volunteers around the world. By August, they had a working [[prototype]] and asked Anna to be their first [[tester]]. She wrote a careful [[test case]] for the sign-up process and found three bugs in ten minutes. Lisa suggested a premium [[add-on]] that would alert users when their favorite books became available. Sofia then created a simple [[landing page]] that explained the idea in two sentences. A week later, a developer from Canada fixed one of their bugs and became their first outside [[contributor]].

c1-33.title: When the website crashed
c1-33.story: On the morning of the online school concert, Max noticed that the livestream site was barely loading. Viewers complained about terrible [[lag]], and the video kept freezing while the [[buffer]] slowly refilled. Max first told everyone to clear their browser [[cache]], but that didn't help. He then logged into the [[web server]] and saw thousands of requests coming from a single [[IP]] address. Someone's broken script was flooding the site, so he added a rule to the [[firewall]] to block it. Meanwhile, Anna called the hosting company, which confirmed that their [[data center]] was working normally. To be safe, Max pointed the school's [[domain]] to a backup machine for the afternoon. Within twenty minutes, the [[real-time]] chat was full of happy comments again. Afterward, Ira joked that next year they should just share the recording over a [[peer-to-peer]] network.

c1-34.title: Working with big data
c1-34.story: Anna joined a summer workshop in [[data science]] at her university in Kyiv. On the first day, the instructor explained how companies use [[big data]] to predict what customers will buy. Anna's team received a [[dataset]] of bike rentals across the city from the past five years. Her laptop was far too slow, so they moved the work to a cloud [[computing]] service. They split the records into smaller chunks and processed one [[batch]] every hour. Max, who was helping, typed a [[prompt]] into an AI tool to get ideas for charts. The animated map they made looked amazing, though its [[rendering]] took most of the night. At the final presentation, a guest from a local company praised their work and asked whether they would consider a career in [[high tech]]. Anna smiled and said she would think about it after a long nap.

c1-35.title: Game day in America
c1-35.story: Lisa spent a month with her cousin in Ohio and sent Anna daily messages about American sports. Her uncle turned out to be a real [[fanatic]] who painted his face before every football game. On Saturday they went to a high school game, where the [[quarterback]] was only seventeen but threw like a professional. The local team was the [[underdog]], since half of its [[roster]] was injured. Still, with ten seconds left, they scored a [[touchdown]] and the crowd went wild. The next day, Lisa watched a baseball game and saw her first [[home run]] fly over the fence. In the evening, a tall boy at the park basketball court finished a pickup game with a spectacular [[dunk]]. Before leaving, Lisa even tried [[lacrosse]] and decided it was the hardest sport of all. She wrote to Anna that she was coming back with a sore arm and a new favorite team.

c1-36.title: At the boxing gym
c1-36.story: Max signed up for classes at a boxing gym near his apartment. The coach, whom everyone called [[sensei]] because he also taught karate, began every session with ten minutes of [[stretching]]. After a month, Max was finally allowed to try [[sparring]] with a partner. His partner was Ira's older cousin, the gym's [[champ]], who had not lost a fight in two years. Max felt like a nervous [[challenger]] and spent most of the round protecting his face. Afterward, a muscular guy in the locker room bragged about his [[six-pack]] and hinted that he took [[steroids|steroid]]. The coach overheard him and gave a strict speech about how [[doping]] ruins both health and careers. Max went home tired and sore, but proud that he had survived his first real fight.
